failure_modes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1: 'there is no information in the passages about "The Calling (2009 film)" or who played the character Hunt in that film.' Summary 2: 'The passages do not contain any information about "The Calling (2009 film)", the character Hunt, or which actor played that role.' Neither summary names the specific missing entity (the film title 'The Calling (2009)' or the cast information for that film) in a way that gives retrieval a concrete target to chase.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Query 2: 'Who played Hunt in "The Calling (2009 film)" and what television series is this actor best known for?' and Query 3: 'Who played Hunt in "The Calling" 2009 film and what television series is this actor best known for?' Both queries are natural-language yes/no questions bundling multiple information requests (identity of actor + television series + best-known role) rather than structured entity lookups.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Query 2: 'Who played Hunt in "The Calling (2009 film)" and what television series is this actor best known for?' Query 3: 'Who played Hunt in "The Calling" 2009 film and what television series is this actor best known for?' The queries are essentially identical (only trivial punctuation differences) and the retrieval returns largely duplicate documents across hops 2 and 3 (Tony Nikolakopoulos, Aaron Paul, John Shepherd, John Hart, Best Actor, Matthew Knight, James Bate all appear in both).

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: The summaries explicitly name the missing entity: Summary 1 states 'there is no information in the passages about "The Calling (2009 film)"' and Summary 2 repeats 'The passages do not contain any information about "The Calling (2009 film)"'. Both Query 2 and Query 3 directly target this entity: 'Who played Hunt in "The Calling (2009 film)"'. Despite well-formed targeting, no passages about The Calling (2009 film) were retrieved across any of the three hops, indicating a corpus/retrieval coverage gap.
